text:
jen: FYI release v2.14.0 promotion is blocked — staging integration suite failing consistently on the session-reuse test
alex: saw that, looks like it started with the last staging deploy around 02:14 UTC
maria: logs show the test failing with timeouts and then the runner hitting ephemeral disk full in the middle of the test run
jen: ugh, disk full? is that the ephemeral runner or the test fixture?
sam: ephemeral runner; `/tmp` fills up because a flaky cleanup job doesn't delete some large artifacts during the test
jen: can we just re-run the pipeline for now to confirm it's not a transient?
ci-bot: deploybot started pipeline `staging/integration-suite` (#4527) on request from jen
ci-bot: job `integration.session-reuse` failed: exit code 2
jen: re-run failed same place. attaching the tail of the log:
```
ERROR: connection timed out waiting for session reattach
/tmp/artifacts/trace-2026-03-20.tar.gz: write failed: no space left on device
Traceback (most recent calls): ...
```
maria: looks like two issues: the flaky cleanup leaves artifact bundles, and the canonical cleanup cron hasn't run because the k8s job controller hit a quota error yesterday and never rescheduled
alex: I can patch the test to avoid writing big artifacts while we investigate, but that means we need a pin or hotfix branch for the release if we want to promote
jenn: (typo) jen: tagging liz — we need a release decision. change window ends in 3h. Do we hold, rollback, or hotfix?
liz: I'm leaning hold unless we have a confirmed safe manual promote plan. Rolling back now will push release to next change window which will cause SLA risk for the customer rollout tonight
sam: alternative: do a manual promote of the build artifact from the previous stable canary (v2.13.9) for the affected routes, while we fix staging infra. That requires pinning service tags and a quick release note update
jen: what's the risk of manual promote? any DB migrations or schema changes between 2.13.9 and 2.14.0?
alex: no schema changes. Main diffs are model config and batching. Rolling forward will be safe, but customers expect the new features. Ops wise manual promote is doable: `deploybot promote --artifact sha:ab12cd34 --target=canary,staging --force`
deploy-bot: promotion attempt blocked: artifact `sha:ab12cd34` not found in remote registry for staging region. (error code: 404_ARTIFACT_MISS)
jen: hm registry lookup is failing for that SHA specifically. Could be GC or replication lag
maria: registry shows both blobs present but the manifest for that tag is missing in the staging region mirror. Ops said there was a mirror sync issue earlier today
liz: given the mirror/registry weirdness, manual promote might be fragile. Proposal: hold promotion, open a short incident to fix registry mirror and trigger a targeted cleanup + re-run after mirror healthy. If mirror can't be healthy within 90 minutes, do a rollback to v2.13.9 via a global revert (requires change window approval)
alex: +1 to incident. I'll prepare a minimal hotfix branch that strips artifact bundling from the failing test and bump the pipeline to avoid writing large tarballs. If incident resolves quickly we can run that and promote same window
sam: I'll draft a release note blurb and a one-line customer advisory for the rollout page in case we need to delay: "Deployment paused due to staging test infra; investigating storage mirror replication. No customer impact observed yet."
jen: action items: alex create hotfix PR and tag `hotfix/v2.14.0-no-artifacts`; sam prepare rollback playbook and release note; liz coordinate change window and decide after 90m; ops to own registry mirror incident and update in #incidents
liz: I'll keep this thread as source of truth. If ops confirms mirror healthy before 90m, we try the hotfix promote. If not, we schedule rollback in next change window.
maria: +1. ops ping: @ops-team can we get an ETA on the mirror resync?
ci-bot: incident created: MIRROR-REPL-321, assigned to ops-team, initial ETA 45 minutes
liz: thanks. tagging this thread for the release board. updating release notes draft with the pause. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jen: ok standing by. I'll update if anything changes. :thumbsup:
